rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence supplies an elided conjunction: ‘nor among the polytheists.’
rows.anchor: التقدير ولا من المشركين. وعم الذين كفروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in ‘those who disbelieve’ is generic, then the verse specifies Jews, Christians, and idolaters rather than a particular group.
rows.anchor: ثم بين أجناسهم من اليهود والنصارى وعبدة الأوثان ليبين في الألف واللام في الذين أنها ليست للعهد يراد بها معين

words: ما يود الذين كفروا من خير من ربكم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commanded honoring of the Prophet is a good bestowed by God that disbelievers do not wish for; the wording then includes every other kind of good.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الآية أن ما أمرناكم به من أن تعظموا نبيكم خير من الله منحكم إياه،

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some treat أن plus the verb as a verbal noun and take من as extra.
rows.anchor: وأن مع الفعل بتأويل المصدر، ومن زائدة في قول بعضهم.

rows.speaker: سيبويه والخليل
rows.claim: Sibawayh and al-Khalil allow the extra من here because denied wishing for good functions like an explicit negation, where it must precede من.
rows.anchor: قام ذلك مقام الجحد الذي يلزم أن يتقدم من الزائدة على قول سيبويه والخليل.

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash permits من to be extra even in an affirmative construction.
rows.anchor: وأما الأخفش فيجيز زيادتها في الواجب

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some take من partitivally: disbelievers wish that no small or great amount of good descend on believers; denying even a portion rules out the whole more strongly.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: من للتبعيض لأنهم يريدون أن لا ينزل على المؤمنين من الخير قليل ولا كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mercy here broadly covers every kind God has granted His servants in past and present.
rows.anchor: والرحمة في هذه الآية عامة لجميع أنواعها التي قد منحها الله عباده قديما وحديثا

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some identify the mercy specifically as the Qur’an; Ibn ʿAṭiyya treats that as one part of the broader mercy.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: الرحمة هي القرآن،

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some identify the mercy as Muhammad’s prophethood, likewise a part of the general mercy in the verse.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: نبوة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، وهذه أجزاء الرحمة العامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, naskh can mean transfer or removal; transfer is not the sense here, while removal is the verse’s sense.
rows.anchor: النسخ في كلام العرب على وجهين: أحدهما النقل كنقل كتاب من آخر، والثاني الإزالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transfer sense is absent here but occurs in 45:29, ‘We had been copying down what you did.’
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: إنا كنا نستنسخ ما كنتم تعملون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Removal may leave the abrogated thing’s successor in place, like the sun removing shade, or leave nothing, like wind erasing a trace; legal abrogation has both forms.
rows.anchor: وهو منقسم في اللغة على ضربين: أحدهما يثبت الناسخ بعد المنسوخ كقولهم نسخت الشمس الظل، والآخر لا يثبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the true abrogator, though the legal address is called abrogating; Sunni experts define it as a later discourse lifting a ruling that otherwise would have continued.
rows.anchor: والناسخ حقيقة هو الله تعالى، ويسمى الخطاب الشرعي ناسخا إذ به يقع النسخ، وحد الناسخ عند حذاق أهل السنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abrogation is rationally possible for God because it entails neither impossibility nor change in His attributes; commands are not tied to will, and God knows each ruling’s endpoint in advance.
rows.anchor: والنسخ جائز على الله تعالى عقلا لأنه ليس يلزم عنه محال ولا تغيير صفة من صفاته تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abrogation does not arise from newly acquired knowledge or a changed divine will; those would imply change that is impossible for God.
rows.anchor: وليست الأوامر متعلقة بالإرادة فيلزم من النسخ أن الإرادة تغيرت، ولا النسخ لطرو علم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Badaʾ is impossible for God because it requires new knowledge or changed will; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says Jews wrongly equated it with abrogation and thereby erred.
rows.anchor: والبداء لا يجوز على الله تعالى لأنه لا يكون إلا لطرو علم

rows.speaker: اليهود
rows.claim: The Jews treated abrogation and badaʾ as one thing and rejected both; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says this was a mistake.
rows.anchor: وجعلت اليهود النسخ والبداء واحدا، ولذلك لم يجوزوه فضلوا

rows.speaker: أئمتنا
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya’s Sunni imams say the abrogated object is the very established ruling itself.
rows.anchor: والمنسوخ عند أئمتنا: الحكم الثابت نفسه

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilites say abrogation removes the equivalent ruling for future cases, based on their doctrines that commands are intended and goodness is intrinsic; Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects those premises.
rows.anchor: لا ما ذهبت إليه المعتزلة، من أنه مثل الحكم الثابت فيما يستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Specification can resemble abrogation but is not: the specified item was never included in the general wording; removing something certainly included would be abrogation.
rows.anchor: والتخصيص من العموم يوهم أنه نسخ وليس به، لأن المخصص لم يتناوله العموم قط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abrogation applies only to commands and prohibitions, not reports; an apparent command-as-report objection is answered by its implicit proviso that God may lift it.
rows.anchor: والنسخ لا يجوز في الإخبار، وإنما هو مختص بالأوامر والنواهي

rows.speaker: بعض المعترضين
rows.claim: A critic begins an objection by treating an order as a report and asking whether it means an obligation to do something.
rows.anchor: ورد بعض المعترضين الأمر خبرا بأن قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection says a command means ‘it is obligatory that you do this’; Ibn ʿAṭiyya replies that it implicitly includes ‘unless I abrogate and lift it.’
rows.anchor: «واجب عليكم أن تفعلوا كذا» ؟ فهذا خبر، والجواب أن يقال: إن في ضمن المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abrogation may move from a heavier rule to a lighter one, from lighter to heavier, between equal burdens, or remove a rule without replacement.
rows.anchor: فقد ينسخ الأثقل إلى الأخف كنسخ الثبوت لعشرة بالثبوت لاثنين، وقد ينسخ الأخف إلى الأثقل

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
rows.claim: As an example of abrogating both recitation and ruling, Ibn ʿAṭiyya cites Abu Bakr’s report of a former recitation declaring disavowal of fathers to be unbelief.
rows.anchor: قول أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه: «كنا نقرأ لا ترغبوا عن آبائكم فإنه كفر»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recitation can be lifted while the rule remains, as with the stoning verse.
rows.anchor: وقد تنسخ التلاوة دون الحكم كآية الرجم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ruling can be lifted while recitation remains, as with the alms before private consultation and 60:11 concerning emigrant wives.
rows.anchor: وقد ينسخ الحكم دون التلاوة كصدقة النجوى،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recitation and ruling are each rulings, so either may be abrogated without the other.
rows.anchor: والتلاوة والحكم حكمان، فجائز نسخ أحدهما دون الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’an may abrogate Qur’an and Sunna Sunna by definitive mass-transmitted reports; abrogation by one-person reports is also agreed when the report abrogates another such report.
rows.anchor: وينسخ القرآن بالقرآن، والسنة بالسنة، وهذه العبارة يراد بها الخبر المتواتر القطعي

rows.speaker: حذاق الأئمة
rows.claim: Leading scholars allow Sunna to abrogate Qur’an, citing ‘no bequest to an heir’; this is apparent in Malik, while al-Shafiʿi denies it, though the stoning rule’s exemption from flogging rests on Sunna.
rows.anchor: وأبى ذلك الشافعي رحمه الله، والحجة عليه من قوله إسقاطه الجلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’an may abrogate Sunna: the Jerusalem direction was not in the Qur’an, and 60:10 bars returning emigrant women after their return had been allowed under the Prophet’s pact with Quraysh.
rows.anchor: وكذلك حذاق الأئمة على أن السنة تنسخ بالقرآن، وذلك موجود في القبلة

rows.speaker: أبو المعالي وغيره
rows.claim: Experts allow Qur’an to be abrogated by a solitary report in principle; Abu al-Maʿali and others say it occurred when a report at Quba announced the change of qibla, while others deny occurrence.
rows.anchor: فذهب أبو المعالي وغيره إلى وقوعه في نازلة مسجد قباء في التحول إلى القبلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Analogy cannot abrogate an explicit text because a valid analogy must not contradict a text.
rows.anchor: ولا يصح نسخ نص بقياس إذ من شروط القياس أن لا يخالف نصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abrogation occurred only during the Prophet’s lifetime; after his death and the law’s stabilization, consensus says it ceased, and a consensus apparently contrary to text must rest on an unknown abrogating text.
rows.anchor: وأما بعد موته واستقرار الشرع فأجمعت الأمة أنه لا نسخ

rows.speaker: بعض المتكلمين
rows.claim: Some theologians say an abrogating rule takes effect for everyone whether or not they know of it.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المتكلمين: «النسخ الثابت متقرر في جهة كل أحد

rows.speaker: حذاق الأئمة
rows.claim: Experts say someone who has not received the abrogating text remains bound by the first ruling until it reaches them.
rows.anchor: والذي عليه الحذاق أنه من لم يبلغه الناسخ فهو متعبد بالحكم الأول

rows.speaker: حذاق الأئمة
rows.claim: Experts permit abrogating a ruling before it is acted upon, as in the story of the intended sacrifice.
rows.anchor: والحذاق على جواز نسخ الحكم قبل فعله، وهو موجود في كتاب الله تعالى

rows.speaker: جمهور الناس
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce ننسخ with an open initial ن, from نسخ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس «ما ننسخ» بفتح النون، من نسخ

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAmir alone among the seven readers uses a damma on the initial ن; Abu ʿAli al-Farisi rejects treating أنسخ as a synonym or causative form, and understands it as ‘find it abrogated.’
rows.anchor: وبها قرأ ابن عامر وحده من السبعة، قال أبو علي الفارسي: ليست لغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the damma reading, Ibn ʿAṭiyya offers either ‘write/reveal from the Preserved Tablet’ or ‘postpone and leave unrevealed’; alternatively it means God permits the Prophet to leave an abrogated verse.
rows.anchor: ما نكتب وننزل من اللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: نافع وحمزة والكسائي وعاصم وابن عامر وجمهور من الناس
rows.claim: These readers pronounce ننسها with a damma on the first ن, a silent second ن, and kasra on س, without hamza; it is from the causative of ‘forget.’
rows.anchor: فقرأ نافع وحمزة والكسائي وعاصم

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group adds a hamza after س, yielding the sense ‘postpone’; the verb ansaʾa is used for delaying a debt.
rows.anchor: وقرأت ذلك فرقة كما تقدم إلا أنها همزت بعد السين

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: An unassigned group reads with an open first ن and open س, meaning ‘leave’; Makki cites it without attribution, and Abu ʿUbayd al-Bakri reports it from Saʿd, which Ibn ʿAṭiyya thinks may be mistaken.
rows.anchor: وقرأت طائفة «أو ننسها» بفتح النون الأولى وسكون الثانية

rows.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
rows.claim: Saʿd is reported to read تنسها addressing the Prophet; when told Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib read it differently, he retorted that the Qur’an was not revealed to al-Musayyib or his family.
rows.anchor: وقرأ سعد بن أبي وقاص «أو تنسها» على مخاطبة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib is said to read ننسها with the initial ن damma-marked and س bearing kasra.
rows.anchor: إن سعيد بن المسيب يقرؤها بنون أولى مضمومة وسين مكسورة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: A separate report says Saʿid reads تنسها with an initial damma on ت and an open س, deriving it from forgetting.
rows.anchor: وقرأ سعيد بن المسيب فيما ذكر عنه أيضا «أو تنسها» بضم التاء

rows.speaker: الضحاك بن مزاحم وأبو رجاء
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak and Abu Rajaʾ read ننسها with the second ن open and a doubled, kasra-marked س, also deriving it from forgetting.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الضحاك بن مزاحم وأبو رجاء «ننسها» بضم النون الأولى

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وابن عباس وإبراهيم النخعي وعطاء ومجاهد وعبيد بن عمير وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: These authorities read ننسأها with an open ن followed by a silent ن and a hamzated alif, giving the meaning ‘postpone.’
rows.anchor: وقرأ عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه وابن عباس وإبراهيم النخعي وعطاء بن أبي رباح ومجاهد وعبيد ابن عمير وابن كثير وأبو عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The delay reading is illustrated by Arab usage for delaying camels’ watering and lengthening their thirst by a day or more.
rows.anchor: نسأت الإبل عن الحوض أنسؤها نسأ أي أخرتها

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: A group reads the delay form with an open ت to address the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقرأت فرقة مثل هذه القراءة إلا أنها بتاء مفتوحة أولا

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة
rows.claim: Abu Haywa reads the same form with ت damma-marked.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة مثل ذلك إلا أنه ضم التاء أولا

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb reads ننسك, addressing the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي بن كعب «أو ننسك» بضم النون الأولى

rows.speaker: سالم مولى أبي حذيفة
rows.claim: Salim’s codex has Ubayy’s reading with the added pronoun for the verse: ننسكها.
rows.anchor: وفي مصحف سالم مولى أبي حذيفة «أو ننسكها» مثل قراءة أبي

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads ‘what We cause you to forget of a verse or abrogate’ and bring its equivalent; Ibn Masʿud’s codex records this wording.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش «ما ننسك من آية أو ننسخها نجىء بمثلها»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya groups the readings under three senses: postponement, causing forgetfulness, or leaving/abandoning.
rows.anchor: وهذه القراءات لا تخلو كل واحدة منها أن تكون من النسء أو الإنساء بمعنى التأخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic nisyān usually means the opposite of remembering but can also mean leaving something.
rows.anchor: والنسيان في كلام العرب يجيء في الأغلب ضد الذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the forgetfulness sense, God may cause the Prophet to forget a verse so it is removed entirely, then provide something better or equal in benefit.
rows.anchor: ما ننسخ من آية أو نقدر نسيانك لها فتنساها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the leaving sense, God may abrogate a verse or leave it unrevealed, while providing a better or equivalent replacement so the religion remains complete.
rows.anchor: ما ننسخ على وجوه النسخ أو نترك غير منزل عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second leaving interpretation is to leave its recitation while lifting its ruling; abrogation then removes both recitation and ruling.
rows.anchor: والمعنى الثاني أو نترك تلاوته وإن رفعنا حكمه فيجيء النسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third leaving interpretation is to leave its ruling while lifting its recitation, again making abrogation a removal of both.
rows.anchor: والمعنى الثالث أو نترك حكمه وإن رفعنا تلاوته فالنسخ أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth interpretation is to leave the verse intact in both recitation and ruling; the pronouns in ‘better/equal than it’ then refer only to what was abrogated.
rows.anchor: نتركها غير منسوخة الحكم ولا التلاوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The postponement reading likewise allows four parallels: delay revelation, ruling, or recitation while retaining the other, or defer a verse without abrogating it.
rows.anchor: يحمل على معنى التأخير فإن الآية معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpretations are stronger than others, but Ibn ʿAṭiyya records all because scholars stated or indicated each possibility.
rows.anchor: وبعض هذه المعاني أقوى من بعض، لكن ذكرنا جميعها لأنها تحتمل

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the kasra reading ننسها cannot mean ‘leave,’ since أنسأ does not mean to leave.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: إن القراءة «أو ننسها» بضم النون وسكون الثانية

rows.speaker: أبو علي وغيره
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli and others accept the ‘leave’ sense by construing it as ‘make you leave it.’
rows.anchor: وقال أبو علي وغيره: ذلك متجه لأنه بمعنى نجعلك تتركها

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj rejects interpreting the verse as the Prophet forgetting, arguing that he never forgot Qur’an; he cites 17:86 as proof that God did not take away what He revealed.
rows.anchor: وكذلك ضعف الزجاج أن تحمل الآية على النسيان الذي هو ضد الذكر، وقال

rows.speaker: أبو علي وغيره
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli and others say intended forgetting is possible and occurred, with no essential difference from lifting a verse by abrogation; they read 17:86 as threatening removal of all revelation, not a part.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو علي وغيره: ذلك جائز وقد وقع ولا فرق بين أن ترفع الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya’s preferred position is that God may cause the Prophet to forget what He intends not to preserve as Qur’an.
rows.anchor: والصحيح في هذا أن نسيان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما أراد الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is protected from human lapses before conveying revelation and after conveyance until a Companion has memorized it; once it is preserved by a Companion, ordinary forgetfulness is possible because the trust has been delivered.
rows.anchor: فالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم معصوم منه قبل التبليغ وبعد التبليغ ما لم يحفظه أحد

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet omitted a verse in prayer, asked whether Ubayy was present, and explained that he had forgotten it rather than it being abrogated; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: لم ترفع ولكني نسيتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khayr is comparative: more beneficial now if the replacement is lighter, in the afterlife if heavier, or equally beneficial if the replacement is equivalent.
rows.anchor: ولفظة خير في الآية صفة تفضيل، والمعنى بأنفع لكم أيها الناس في عاجل إن كانت الناسخة أخف

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some take خير as a verbal noun and من as marking origin.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم «خير» في الآية مصدر و «من» لابتداء الغاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya finds the verbal-noun analysis strained because ‘or like it’ would need to coordinate with the pronoun in منها without repeating من.
rows.anchor: ويقلق هذا القول لقوله تعالى أو مثلها إلا أن يعطف المثل على الضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although phrased as a question, ألم تعلم functions as confirmation, which like a direct question needs an alternative clause.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: ألم تعلم أن ظاهره الاستفهام ومعناه التقرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some identify the alternative with أم تريدون in 2:18; others treat أم as disconnected and supply ‘or did you know?’; if the Prophet alone is addressed, the alternative is omitted. Both analyses are transmitted.
rows.anchor: فالمعادل هنا على قول جماعة أم تريدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God abrogates or confirms what He wills and acts freely in His rulings; this answers the Jews’ denial of abrogation.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الآية أن الله تعالى ينسخ ما يشاء ويثبت ما يشاء

words: أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Everything’ is general in wording but particular in scope: reason excludes God’s eternal attributes and impossibilities, which are not things.
rows.anchor: على كل شيء لفظ عموم معناه الخصوص، إذ لم تدخل فيه الصفات القديمة بدلالة العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, a thing means an existent.
rows.anchor: والشيء في كلام العرب الموجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qadīr is an intensive active participle from qadara–yaqdiru; some Arabs instead say qadara–yaqdiru with the opposite vowel pattern.
rows.anchor: وقدير اسم فاعل على المبالغة من «قدر» بفتح العين «يقدر»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening means ‘remember when’; qawāʿid is the plural of qāʿida, meaning a foundation.
rows.anchor: واذكر إذ، والقواعد جمع قاعدة وهي الأساس

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ says the foundations are the walls; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls this figurative usage.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: «هي الجدر» . قال القاضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammarians explain the feminine form qāʿida as the woman who has ceased bearing children; some say its feminine tāʾ drops because there is no masculine counterpart, while al-Khalil treats it as a relational adjective, not verbal agreement.
rows.anchor: والقواعد من النساء جمع قاعد وهي التي قعدت عن الولد، وحذفت تاء التأنيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The House in this passage is the Kaʿba by consensus.
rows.anchor: والبيت هنا الكعبة بإجماع

rows.speaker: بعض رواة القصص
rows.claim: One story says Adam built the House on God’s command, it later disappeared, and Abraham found and raised its foundations; other accounts say it descended from Paradise as a pearl or ruby, or that the earth spread from beneath a red or white mound before Abraham began the building.
rows.anchor: فقيل إن آدم أمر ببنائه، فبناه، ثم دثر ودرس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What is sound is that God commanded Abraham to raise the foundations; the House may have existed earlier or this may have been its first construction, and neither account can be preferred without conclusive transmission.
rows.anchor: والذي يصح من هذا كله أن الله أمر إبراهيم برفع قواعد البيت

rows.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr says Abraham and Ishmael raised the foundations together.
rows.anchor: وقال عبيد بن عمير: رفعها إبراهيم وإسماعيل معا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Abraham raised the foundations while Ishmael handed him stones.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: رفعها إبراهيم، وإسماعيل يناوله الحجارة

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: A report attributed to ʿAli says Abraham raised the foundations while Ishmael was a small child; Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects its attribution as contradicted by the verse and reports.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب: رفعها إبراهيم، وإسماعيل طفل صغير. قال القاضي أبو محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishmael may be coordinated with Abraham or treated as a new subject whose predicate comes later.
rows.anchor: وإسماعيل عطف على إبراهيم، وقيل هو مقطوع على الابتداء وخبره فيما بعد

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi derives Ismāʿīl from ‘hear, O El.’
rows.anchor: قال الماوردي: إسماعيل أصله اسمع يا إيل

rows.speaker: طائفة
rows.claim: One group understands the prophets’ request for repentance as asking for steadfastness and its continuance.
rows.anchor: فقالت طائفة: طلبا التثبيت والدوام

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Another view makes the request concern their descendants, as when someone asks that a blessing be given to them but means their children and descendants.
rows.anchor: أرادا من بعدهما من الذرية كما تقول برني فلان وأكرمني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers that Abraham and Ishmael sought to establish those rites and places as sites where people could repent and seek release from sin.
rows.anchor: وقيل وهو الأحسن عندي: إنهما لما عرفا المناسك وبنيا البيت

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari says no creature’s relationship with God is such that it could not be better than it is.
rows.anchor: وقال الطبري: إنه ليس أحد من خلق الله تعالى إلا وبينه وبين الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The community agrees that prophets are protected in conveying revelation, from major sins, and from disgraceful minor sins; scholars dispute other minor sins, but Ibn ʿAṭiyya holds that prophets are protected from all of them.
rows.anchor: وأجمعت الأمة على عصمة الأنبياء في معنى التبليغ ومن الكبائر ومن الصغائر التي فيها رذيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s daily repentance seventy times is a return from one spiritual state to a higher one as his knowledge and awareness increase; repentance here is lexical in sense.
rows.anchor: إنما هو رجوعه من حالة إلى أرفع منها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet referred to this prayer when he said, ‘I am the supplication of my father Abraham and the good news of Jesus.’
rows.anchor: هذا هو الذي أراد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بقوله «أنا دعوة أبي إبراهيم، وبشرى عيسى»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘From among them’ means that the messenger would be known to them, his merit recognized, and he would show them concern, compassion, and care.
rows.anchor: ومعنى منهم أن يعرفوه ويتحققوا فضله ويشفق عليهم ويحرص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يَتْلُوا may be an accusative adjective describing messenger as one reciting to them, or a circumstantial clause.
rows.anchor: في موضع نصب نعت لرسول أي تاليا عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs and the Book are the Qur’an; the Prophet is credited with teaching because he supplies what people investigate and teaches methods of inquiry through what God reveals to him.
rows.anchor: والآيات آيات القرآن، والكتاب القرآن، ونسب التعليم إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada identifies wisdom as the Sunna and the Prophet’s explanation of the legal rulings.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: الحكمة السنة وبيان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الشرائع

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik, as transmitted by Ibn Wahb, identifies wisdom as religious understanding and an inborn comprehension and light from God.
rows.anchor: وروى ابن وهب عن مالك: أن الحكمة الفقه في الدين والفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yuzakkīhim means to purify them and cultivate them in goodness; zakāt’s sense does not go beyond purification or growth.
rows.anchor: ويزكيهم معناه يطهرهم وينميهم بالخير، ومعنى الزكاة لا يخرج عن التطهير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿAzīz is the one who overcomes, whose will is carried out and not repelled; al-Ḥakīm places actions correctly and makes them precise.
rows.anchor: والعزيز الذي يغلب ويتم مراده ولا يرد، والحكيم المصيب مواقع الفعل المحكم لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kataba here means prescribed and established; writing is often used for lasting, enduring matters.
rows.anchor: كتب معناه فرض وأثبت، والكتب مستعمل في الأمور المخلدات الدائمة كثيرا

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some say ‘prescribed’ reports what was written in the Preserved Tablet and settled by prior decree.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن كتب في مثل هذا إخبار عما كتب في اللوح المحفوظ وسبق به القضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The killer must submit to lawful retaliation if the victim’s guardian seeks it; the guardian must not kill anyone beyond the killer; rulers must enforce retaliation and prescribed penalties.
rows.anchor: وصورة فرض القصاص هو أن القاتل فرض عليه إذا أراد الولي القتل الاستسلام لأمر الله

words: فَمَنْ عُفِيَ لَهُ مِنْ أَخِيهِ شَىْءٌ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Retaliation is not compulsory when the parties agree to blood money or pardon; the binding limit is not to exceed retaliation, which is the endpoint when they dispute.
rows.anchor: وليس القصاص بلزام إنما اللزام أن لا يتجاوز القصاص إلى اعتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qiṣāṣ derives from tracing footsteps: the killer has followed a path of killing, and retaliation follows that same path.
rows.anchor: والقصاص مأخوذ من قص الأثر فكأن القاتل سلك طريقا من القتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-qatlā is a plural of qatīl in a collective feminine form; this pattern is used for things that befall people against their will, like wounded, ill, or drowned people.
rows.anchor: والقتلى جمع قتيل، لفظ مؤنث تأنيث الجماعة وهو مما يدخل على الناس كرها

words: ٱلْحُرُّ بِٱلْحُرِّ وَٱلْعَبْدُ بِٱلْعَبْدِ وَٱلْأُنثَىٰ بِٱلْأُنثَىٰ
rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says the verse addressed an Arab custom in which powerful clans killed a free person for a slain slave or a man for a slain woman.
rows.anchor: فقال الشعبي: إن العرب كان أهل العزة منهم والمنعة إذا قتل منهم عبد قتلوا به حرا

rows.speaker: قوم من العرب
rows.claim: Another account says Arab groups fought a confused battle and threatened to kill free men in retaliation for their slaves, prompting the verse.
rows.anchor: وحكي أن قوما من العرب تقاتلوا قتال عمية ثم قال بعضهم: نقتل بعبيدنا أحرارا، فنزلت الآية

words: ٱلْحُرُّ بِٱلْحُرِّ وَٱلْعَبْدُ بِٱلْعَبْدِ وَٱلْأُنثَىٰ بِٱلْأُنثَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reported occasion involved fighting between two Anṣar tribes, or other tribes, in which men, slaves, and women were killed; the Prophet ordered reconciliation and equal blood money by class.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نزلت بسبب قتال وقع بين قبيلتين من الأنصار، وقيل: من غيرهم فقتل هؤلاء

words: ٱلْحُرُّ بِٱلْحُرِّ وَٱلْعَبْدُ بِٱلْعَبْدِ وَٱلْأُنثَىٰ بِٱلْأُنثَىٰ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the verse first barred killing a man for a woman, a woman for a man, or one social class for another, then was abrogated by 5:45, ‘a life for a life.’
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أن الآية نزلت مقتضية أن لا يقتل الرجل بالمرأة

words: ٱلْحُرُّ بِٱلْحُرِّ وَٱلْعَبْدُ بِٱلْعَبْدِ وَٱلْأُنثَىٰ بِٱلْأُنثَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’an 5:45 reports what was prescribed for the Israelites; it only abrogates this rule for Muslims if a report from the Prophet establishes that their law also governs us.
rows.anchor: وآية المائدة إنما هي إخبار عما كتب على بني إسرائيل، فلا يترتب النسخ إلا بما تلقي عن رسول الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, as cited by Abu ʿUbayd, and others say the verse remains operative in general terms, with 5:45 explaining its generality.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس فيما ذكر أبو عبيد وعن غيره أن هذه الآية محكمة وفيها إجمال

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says ‘the free for the free’ includes both men and women.
rows.anchor: وأن قوله هنا الحر بالحر يعم الرجال والنساء، وقاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik’s preferred explanation treats male and female as one gender category; repeating ‘female’ emphasizes concern to end the pre-Islamic custom.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك رحمه الله: أحسن ما سمعت في هذه الآية أنه يراد بها الجنس الذكر

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب والحسن
rows.claim: A report from ʿAli and al-Hasan says that when a man kills a woman, her heirs may execute him while paying half the blood money, or spare him and take her full blood money; reciprocal options apply when a woman kills a man.
rows.anchor: وروي عن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه وعن الحسن بن أبي الحسن أن الآية نزلت مبينة حكم المذكورين

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب والحسن
rows.claim: The same report says that if a free man kills a slave, the owner may have him killed while paying the free man’s blood money minus the slave’s value, or spare him and take the slave’s value.
rows.anchor: وإذا قتل الحر العبد فإن أراد سيد العبد قتل وأعطى دية الحر إلا قيمة العبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reports assigning the unequal blood-money options to ʿAli and al-Hasan were also denied; the community agrees that a man may be executed for a woman and a woman for a man, while most deny a blood-money offset and others allow it.
rows.anchor: وقد أنكر ذلك عنهما أيضا، وأجمعت الأمة على قتل الرجل بالمرأة

rows.speaker: مالك والشافعي
rows.claim: Malik and al-Shafiʿi allow reciprocal retaliation between men and women for injuries below homicide.
rows.anchor: قال مالك والشافعي: وكذلك القصاص بينهما فيما دون النفس

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa allows no retaliation between men and women for injuries below homicide, only for life against life.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة: لا قصاص بينهما فيما دون النفس

rows.speaker: النخعي وقتادة وسعيد بن المسيب والشعبي والثوري وأبو حنيفة ومحمد بن الحسن وأبو يوسف
rows.claim: Al-Nakhaʿi, Qatada, Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib, al-Shaʿbi, al-Thawri, Abu Hanifa, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and Abu Yusuf say a free person may be executed for killing a slave.
rows.anchor: وقال النخعي وقتادة وسعيد بن المسيب والشعبي والثوري وأبو حنيفة ومحمد بن الحسن وأبو يوسف

rows.speaker: مالك وجمهور من العلماء
rows.claim: Malik and most scholars say a free person is not executed for a slave: they cite the slave’s unequal status in lesser injuries, the rule of value-only compensation for accidental killing, and the slave’s status as property.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك رحمه الله وجمهور من العلماء: لا يقتل الحر بالعبد

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: In Malik’s school, a father who clearly and deliberately kills his son without plausible mistake is executed; if he kills by an ordinary blow or throw, two positions either impose retaliation or spare him with aggravated blood money.
rows.anchor: وإذا قتل الرجل ابنه فإن قصد إلى قتله مثل أن يضجعه ويذبحه أو يصبره
